deck: Set 1: Solution Design, Problem Framing & Architecture
term: Four Evaluation Pillars (Efficiency, Transformation, Solution Cost, Performance SLA)
definition:
Anthropic architectural evaluation framework separating:
• **Efficiency**: Doing existing tasks faster or with fewer manual hours.
• **Transformation**: Enabling new capabilities or business workflows previously impossible.
• **Solution Cost**: Total cost of ownership (input/output tokens, caching, retrieval, human review, infrastructure).
• **Performance SLA**: Hard latency (TTFT, P95/P99 completion), availability, and accuracy targets.
examTip: If an architecture fails a hard **Performance SLA** (e.g., clinical or regulatory latency bound), eliminate it first before comparing Efficiency and Solution Cost.

deck: Set 1: Solution Design, Problem Framing & Architecture
term: Deterministic Code vs. Claude Judgment Boundary
definition: Claude should handle unstructured text interpretation, synthesis, classification, and ambiguous routing, while **deterministic application code** must own exact calculations (e.g., tax/pricing math), schema validation, state mutations, and access control.
examTip: Never encode tax math, financial calculations, or hard eligibility rules purely inside a system prompt—delegate those to deterministic code or verified tools.

deck: Set 1: Solution Design, Problem Framing & Architecture
definition:
Tailor architecture artifacts to each stakeholder's decision rights:
• **Security & Compliance**: Threat model, residual-risk register, control-mapping table.
• **Product Manager**: Delivered capabilities, feature-level roadmap dependencies.
• **Delivery / Engineering**: Component diagrams, interface contracts, configuration parameters, operational runbooks.
• **Executive Sponsor**: Business outcome, ROI/cost, risk summary, and decision options.
examTip: Avoid sending a single undifferentiated narrative to all audiences; match artifacts to each role's governance or implementation responsibilities.

deck: Set 1: Solution Design, Problem Framing & Architecture
term: Invoice & Document Pipeline Layering (Pre-Processing, Model Stage, Post-Processing)
definition:
• **Pre-Processing**: OCR on scanned images, authentication/authorization checks, and PII redaction prior to model invocation.
• **Model Stage**: Claude-based classification of document type and structured field extraction.
• **Post-Processing**: Deterministic JSON schema validation and persistence of validated records to the system of record.
examTip: PII redaction and auth checks must execute in **Pre-Processing** before retrieval or model invocation; schema validation and DB persistence belong in **Post-Processing**.

deck: Set 1: Solution Design, Problem Framing & Architecture
definition: Before introducing Claude, decompose end-to-end process latency. If 80% of delay comes from an overnight batch sync and 20% from manual note triage, fix the system sync in the platform and scope Claude specifically to note extraction—measuring both metrics independently.
examTip: Never ask Claude to 'infer' missing system state to work around a broken database synchronization.

deck: Set 2: Agentic Workflows & Multi-Agent Orchestration
definition:
• **Prompt Chaining (Fixed Pipeline)**: Best when steps are known in advance (e.g., Extract -> Validate -> Synthesize) with programmatic gates between stages.
• **Orchestrator-Workers (Dynamic Decomposition)**: Best when subtasks depend on runtime discoveries (e.g., multi-file bug investigation), using bounded task contracts.
examTip: Prefer the simplest deterministic workflow that meets the requirement; only use dynamic multi-agent orchestration when task topology cannot be known upfront.

deck: Set 2: Agentic Workflows & Multi-Agent Orchestration
definition: Subagents run in isolated context windows and do **not** automatically inherit the parent coordinator's full conversation history. The coordinator dispatches bounded tasks with explicit input payloads and receives structured summary artifacts back.
examTip: Use subagents to prevent context pollution when analyzing large independent partitions (e.g., separate hospital wards or annexes) in parallel.

deck: Set 2: Agentic Workflows & Multi-Agent Orchestration
term: Coupled State vs. Parallel Task Decomposition
definition: Tasks with tightly coupled shared constraints (e.g., resource scheduling where every allocation immediately constrains all others) should remain with a **single context owner** rather than split across independent parallel agents that create conflicting allocations.
examTip: Parallelize independent evidence-gathering or verification, but keep coupled constraint solving under one authoritative coordinator/context owner.

deck: Set 2: Agentic Workflows & Multi-Agent Orchestration
definition:
• **`tool_use`**: Execute the requested client tool(s) and return `tool_result` blocks in the next user message.
• **`pause_turn`**: Server-side loop paused on a long turn; send the assistant content back with a continuation bound.
• **`max_tokens`**: Output was truncated at the token ceiling; treat structured JSON as incomplete and segment or rerun.
examTip: Never parse a `max_tokens`-truncated JSON payload as a complete business record, and never rely solely on natural-language wording when `stop_reason` provides explicit state.

deck: Set 2: Agentic Workflows & Multi-Agent Orchestration
definition: When an agent investigates complex incidents across multiple telemetry tools, maintain a structured hypothesis-evidence graph, dispatch bounded probe tasks for unresolved claims, update state only from verified tool outputs, and stop when acceptance criteria are met.
examTip: Avoid letting multiple agents vote on the full raw transcript without structured evidence linkage.

deck: Set 3: Tool Design, Tool Search & Model Context Protocol (MCP)
definition: When an agent connects to dozens or hundreds of tools across MCP servers, mark low-frequency tools with `defer_loading: true` and enable the Tool Search tool. Claude discovers relevant tools on demand via `tool_reference` without bloating every turn's input token prefix.
examTip: Keep high-frequency core tools loaded in the static prefix and defer specialized/administrative tools via `defer_loading: true`.

deck: Set 3: Tool Design, Tool Search & Model Context Protocol (MCP)
definition: When an agent misroutes calls across 30+ tools, the primary root cause is **overlapping tool descriptions and ambiguous input schemas**. Refactor tool names, descriptions, and boundaries—or split into domain-routed specialist toolsets.
examTip: Adding more tools or speculative 'future' tools degrades tool-selection accuracy; keep an agent's active toolset scoped to its defined tasks and handoffs.

deck: Set 3: Tool Design, Tool Search & Model Context Protocol (MCP)
definition: When a tool invocation fails, return a structured `tool_result` with `is_error: true`, an explicit `errorCategory` (`transient`, `validation`, `permission`, `business_rule`), `isRetryable` boolean, and a safe actionable message.
examTip: Never expose raw stack traces or fallback admin credentials in tool errors, and distinguish retryable transient timeouts from terminal permission/validation errors.

deck: Set 3: Tool Design, Tool Search & Model Context Protocol (MCP)
definition:
• `tool_choice: {"type": "auto"}`: Model decides whether to call a tool.
• `tool_choice: {"type": "any"}`: Model must call at least one tool from the provided list.
• `tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "..."}`: Forces the model to call a specific named tool (ideal for guaranteed structured extraction or first-step lookup).
examTip: Note that Extended Thinking is not compatible with forced `tool_choice: {"type": "any"}` or `{"type": "tool"}`—use `auto` when Extended Thinking is active on that turn.

deck: Set 3: Tool Design, Tool Search & Model Context Protocol (MCP)
definition: External or third-party MCP servers can introduce new tools or change tool behavior during upgrades. Default MCP tool permissions to `always_ask`, explicitly allowlist only vetted read-only tools, and gate destructive/write tools (`close_account`, `delete`) behind human approval.
examTip: Never trust an MCP server's display name as proof that every tool it exposes in future versions is read-only.

deck: Set 4: Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs
definition: When adding few-shot examples for one concern (e.g., business logic bugs) measurably degrades recall on another concern (e.g., API design/security) in a single monolithic prompt, split the review into **separate focused prompts** with dedicated examples and consolidate findings.
examTip: Upgrading to a larger model or adding a longer checklist does not fix attention competition inside a single overloaded prompt.

deck: Set 4: Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs
definition:
• **Zero-Shot**: Ideal starting point when categories, rules, and field contracts are clearly specified and already meet accuracy targets.
• **Few-Shot**: Anchors exact output formatting, edge-case disambiguation, and boundary judgments.
• **Chain-of-Thought / Thinking**: Reserved for multi-step reasoning, constraint satisfaction, and complex synthesis—not needed on simple deterministic extractions where it adds latency and output tokens.
examTip: Do not enable Chain-of-Thought or Extended Thinking by default on every simple classification task where latency SLAs are tight.

deck: Set 4: Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs
definition: If user transcripts or code blocks naturally contain a configured `stop_sequence` delimiter (e.g., `---END---`), generation terminates prematurely with `stop_reason: "stop_sequence"`. Confirm the fired stop sequence, encode or replace colliding delimiters (e.g., XML tags), and verify schema completeness.
examTip: Always inspect `stop_reason` and `stop_sequence` in telemetry when outputs unexpectedly truncate mid-document.

deck: Set 4: Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs
definition: Users frequently ask leading questions containing false premises (e.g., citing a non-existent certificate or policy clause). Prompt and pipeline design must verify premises against retrieved source evidence first, explicitly allow **abstention** when evidence is missing, and surface conflicting sources rather than guessing.
examTip: When sources conflict, instruct Claude to produce an attributed brief preserving both conflicting claims with provenance rather than silently picking one.

deck: Set 4: Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs
term: Nullable Schema Fields vs. Hallucinated Defaults
definition: In structured JSON extraction schemas, make optional or frequently absent fields explicitly **nullable** (`null` or `not_found` enum) so Claude does not fabricate values to satisfy a required string/number constraint.
examTip: Combine nullable schema fields with deterministic post-processing validation before writing to downstream databases.

deck: Set 5: Prompt Caching, Extended Thinking & Token Economics
definition: Prompt caching matches exact prefixes in the order: **`tools` -> `system` -> `messages`**. Place stable, repeated content (tool definitions, system instructions, shared reference manuals, few-shot examples) at the very head of the prompt, and put per-request dynamic variables or user queries at the end.
examTip: Injecting a changing timestamp, request UUID, or user-specific header at the top of the system prompt invalidates the entire downstream cache prefix!

deck: Set 5: Prompt Caching, Extended Thinking & Token Economics
term: Top-Level Automatic Caching in Multi-Turn Sessions
definition: In growing multi-turn conversations, advancing the cache breakpoint across turns allows prior conversation history and tool results to be read from cache (`cache_read_input_tokens`) rather than re-processed at full input price.
examTip: Monitor both `cache_creation_input_tokens` (writes) and `cache_read_input_tokens` (hits) per workload slice to confirm positive cache ROI.

deck: Set 5: Prompt Caching, Extended Thinking & Token Economics
definition: Extended Thinking allocates an internal reasoning budget before emitting the final response. With **Adaptive Thinking**, you can tune the `effort` level (`low`, `medium`, `high`). If `medium` effort meets all quality/constraint gates while meeting P95 latency, adopt it over `high`.
examTip: When continuing an active tool-use loop within the same turn, preserve the assistant's `thinking` blocks alongside `tool_use` blocks; do not copy prior clients' thinking blocks into a new client's session.

deck: Set 5: Prompt Caching, Extended Thinking & Token Economics
term: Streaming & Time To First Token (TTFT) vs. Full Completion SLA
definition: **Streaming** dramatically reduces perceived latency (TTFT) for interactive human chat, but it does **not** reduce total token generation time. If a downstream machine pipeline requires the complete validated JSON within an 8-second SLA, streaming alone will not satisfy the full-completion SLA.
examTip: To reduce full-completion time, shorten output token length, tune thinking effort, ensure high cache-hit rates, or route to a faster qualified model.

deck: Set 5: Prompt Caching, Extended Thinking & Token Economics
definition: Different model families/versions can tokenize the same text into different token counts. Never compare raw token counts as a model-independent efficiency score; use each target model's token-counting endpoint and compare **end-to-end cost and latency per accepted task**.
examTip: Always normalize efficiency metrics to cost per accepted output and P95/P99 latency on the target model.

deck: Set 6: RAG, Chunking, Retrieval & Citations
term: Dense vs. Sparse vs. Hybrid vs. Structured Retrieval
definition:
• **Dense Vector Retrieval**: Captures paraphrased semantic intent over unstructured prose.
• **Sparse Lexical Retrieval (BM25)**: Recovers exact identifiers, SKUs, error codes, and rare tokens.
• **Hybrid Retrieval**: Combines dense + sparse with reciprocal rank fusion / reranking for superior recall.
• **Structured Query (SQL/Metadata)**: Best for exact filter-and-aggregate queries over relational schemas.
examTip: Never use a vector index as a replacement for relational filter/aggregate queries, and always pair dense vectors with sparse lexical search when exact product/clause IDs matter.

deck: Set 6: RAG, Chunking, Retrieval & Citations
definition:
• **Code or Hierarchical Specs**: Function-level, AST, or tree-aware chunking following specification hierarchy.
• **Long Structured Documents**: Semantic chunking along clause/paragraph boundaries or hierarchical section-mirroring chunks.
• **Heterogeneous Short Records**: Per-record chunking (1 record = 1 chunk) or fixed-size with overlap.
examTip: When adding Contextual Retrieval prefixes to chunks, verify that `prefix + chunk` stays within the embedding model's token limit and rebuild both dense and sparse indexes from the same versioned chunk IDs.

deck: Set 6: RAG, Chunking, Retrieval & Citations
definition: Authentication and authorization must run **before** retrieval so the search query enforces hard metadata filters (`tenant_id`, `role`, `product_family`, `major_version`) in the retrieval engine prior to semantic ranking.
examTip: Never retrieve across all tenants and rely on the prompt to tell Claude 'ignore documents belonging to other tenants'.

deck: Set 6: RAG, Chunking, Retrieval & Citations
term: Retrieval Evaluation (`Pass@k` & Golden Chunks) vs. Answer Evaluation
definition:
Separate RAG evaluation into two distinct stages:
1. **Retrieval Eval**: Measure `Pass@k` / recall against golden source chunks before generation.
2. **Generation Eval**: Measure groundedness, citation accuracy, and abstention on verified vs. unverified premises.
examTip: A lucky end-to-end answer does not prove retrieval is healthy; always measure `Pass@k` on campus/year/version edge cases separately.

deck: Set 6: RAG, Chunking, Retrieval & Citations
definition: Enable document citations or structured provenance fields (`source_id`, `document_title`, `section`, `char_location`/`page_number`) so reviewers and downstream UIs can verify every factual claim directly against the authoritative passage.
examTip: When compacting long multi-step research contexts, preserve structured file/citation pointers rather than summarizing away source identifiers.

deck: Set 7: Evaluation, Graders & Experimentation
term: Sample Size & Statistical Power in A/B Testing
definition: Before running a prompt or model experiment, compute required sample size from the baseline rate, minimum detectable effect (MDE), significance level ($\alpha$), and statistical power ($1-\beta$). Do not stop an experiment early on a noisy 1-day dip or declare a winner when exposure logs have sample ratio mismatch.
examTip: If a high-severity slice (e.g., wrongful cancellation) has only 2 events in online traffic, supplement the online A/B test with a dedicated high-volume **offline stratified evaluation set**.

deck: Set 7: Evaluation, Graders & Experimentation
definition: If a single holistic LLM grader favors polite/empathetic tone over factual accuracy, split the rubric into **independent dimensions** (e.g., deterministic/code check for required clauses + calibrated rubric for factual support + separate tone score) and calibrate against human-adjudicated labels.
examTip: Use deterministic code graders whenever outputs can be checked via exact schema, regex, or clause presence, and reserve calibrated model/human graders for semantic quality.

deck: Set 7: Evaluation, Graders & Experimentation
definition:
• **Regression Gate**: High-pass threshold (near 100%) on mature, reliable production workflows that blocks any deployment regressing core behavior.
• **Capability Evals**: Track progress on harder, actively improving workflows without masking regressions in stable slices.
examTip: Never average 4 reliable workflows and 1 experimental workflow into a single combined score that hides regressions on the reliable paths.

deck: Set 7: Evaluation, Graders & Experimentation
term: Capturing Production Dispositions for Flywheel Curation
definition: Log linked traces containing input reference, retrieved evidence, prompt/model version, generated output, and the human reviewer's disposition (`approved`, `edited`, `rejected` with reason). Curate verified failure patterns into versioned offline evaluation suites.
examTip: Never auto-inject unverified raw user corrections directly into production prompts without review and versioned evaluation.

deck: Set 7: Evaluation, Graders & Experimentation
definition: When staging evaluations pass but production grades drop, capture and compare the exact resolved model snapshot ID, provider/region routing, temperature/thinking settings, retrieval index freshness, and input traffic distribution across both environments.
examTip: Never lower the production grader threshold just to make staging and production pass rates match.

deck: Set 8: Batch API, Tiered Routing & Cost Operations
definition: The **Message Batches API** processes asynchronous workloads (up to 24-hour window) at a 50% cost discount without consuming real-time interactive rate limits. Ideal for overnight document backfills, bulk evaluations, and non-urgent catalog enrichment.
term: Message Batches API vs. Synchronous & Priority Tier
examTip: Never use the 24-hour Batch API for synchronous user-blocking requests with strict seconds-level SLAs; use **Priority Tier** or provisioned capacity for critical low-latency spikes.

deck: Set 8: Batch API, Tiered Routing & Cost Operations
definition: Each item in a Message Batch carries a `custom_id`. Inspect each item's result status (`succeeded`, `errored`, `expired`, `canceled`) and `stop_reason` (including `refusal`). Re-submit only failed/expired `custom_id` items after fixing transient or token-limit issues.
examTip: A batch job completing with HTTP 200 does not mean every item produced a usable business answer—always check per-item status and `stop_reason`.

deck: Set 8: Batch API, Tiered Routing & Cost Operations
definition: Route high-volume routine classification or lookup planning to a fast, cost-efficient model (e.g., Claude Haiku/Sonnet) validated against the accuracy contract, and escalate only complex synthesis or low-confidence edge cases to a heavier capability-leading model (e.g., Opus).
examTip: Evaluate each stage's accuracy contract and end-to-end P95 latency including escalation retries before promoting a tiered router.

deck: Set 8: Batch API, Tiered Routing & Cost Operations
definition: Measure P95 and P99 latency from **request admission to the first valid business result** under representative peak concurrency, explicitly accounting for queue wait time, tool-call round-trips, and validation retries.
examTip: First-attempt model latency is misleading if 15% of requests fail schema validation and trigger a second full generation retry.

deck: Set 8: Batch API, Tiered Routing & Cost Operations
term: Workspace Isolation, Usage API & Cost Attribution
definition: Assign separate Anthropic Console **Workspaces** and service-specific API keys per business unit or workload. Reconcile near-real-time Usage buckets with finalized Cost API reports and application-level telemetry.
examTip: Do not share a single API key across multiple departments and attempt to guess cost allocation from aggregate monthly invoices.

deck: Set 9: Claude Code, CLAUDE.md, Skills & Dev Enablement
definition:
Claude Code settings and permissions follow a strict five-level hierarchy:
**1. Managed (Enterprise policy) > 2. Command-line arguments > 3. Local (`.claude/settings.local.json`) > 4. Project (`.claude/settings.json` / `.mcp.json`) > 5. User (`~/.claude/settings.json`)**.
examTip: **Managed** settings sit at the top of the precedence hierarchy and cannot be overridden by user, project, or local configurations. Use **Project scope** for shared team settings committed to git.

deck: Set 9: Claude Code, CLAUDE.md, Skills & Dev Enablement
definition: Commit a concise `CLAUDE.md` at the repository root (and optional `.claude/rules/*.md` with path-scoped glob frontmatter) documenting build/test commands, architectural invariants, and coding conventions so every session loads project context automatically.
examTip: Keep root `CLAUDE.md` focused and high-signal; move domain-specific instructions into path-scoped `.claude/rules/` files or on-demand Skills.

deck: Set 9: Claude Code, CLAUDE.md, Skills & Dev Enablement
term: Claude Code Hooks (`PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse`) vs. Prompt Rules
definition: **Hooks** are deterministic shell/application callbacks that execute at lifecycle points (e.g., `PreToolUse` to block prohibited commands or sensitive paths; `PostToolUse` to run linters/formatters). Use hooks whenever 100% deterministic enforcement is required.
examTip: Prompt instructions in `CLAUDE.md` are advisory; security-critical command blocking and mandatory formatting belong in deterministic **Hooks** and permission rules.

deck: Set 9: Claude Code, CLAUDE.md, Skills & Dev Enablement
definition: Package reusable domain workflows and executable scripts as a **Skill** with a top-level `SKILL.md` (containing valid YAML frontmatter `name` and `description`). In production container requests, pin the exact `skill_id` and `version` rather than floating on 'latest'.
examTip: Skills support progressive disclosure: Claude reads the concise frontmatter description first and loads the full `SKILL.md` and scripts only when relevant.

deck: Set 9: Claude Code, CLAUDE.md, Skills & Dev Enablement
term: Plan Mode vs. Direct Execution in Codebase Refactoring
definition: Use **Plan Mode** first when a task spans multiple modules, requires architectural trade-offs, or has ambiguous scope—allowing the engineer to review and approve the migration plan before edits begin. Use direct execution for well-bounded, single-file fixes with clear test coverage.
examTip: For large repository investigations, start with lightweight path/symbol search (`Grep`/`Glob`) before reading full files into context.

deck: Set 10: Responsible AI, Security, Guardrails & Governance
definition:
Untrusted external content (emails, invoices, web pages, repo issues) can contain adversarial instructions. Defend with:
1. Clear structural delimiters marking untrusted data.
2. Runtime input/output classifiers.
3. Least-privilege tool permissions that cannot be elevated by message content.
4. Mandatory human confirmation (`always_ask`) before external sends or state mutations.
examTip: Never grant users or untrusted documents a privilege level asserted inside natural-language message text.

deck: Set 10: Responsible AI, Security, Guardrails & Governance
term: Fairness Evaluation: Approval Rate Parity vs. Error Rate Parity
definition: Equal approval rates across demographic or regional groups (**approval rate parity**) do **not** prove fairness if false-negative or false-positive error rates differ across groups (**error rate parity**) or if human baseline labels contain historical bias.
examTip: Always evaluate disaggregated error severity, false-refusal/false-rejection rates, and abstention rates across protected groups and language queues.

deck: Set 10: Responsible AI, Security, Guardrails & Governance
term: Fallback Model Safety Invariants on Refusals
definition: If a primary model stops with a safety `refusal`, do **not** blindly fail over to a less-restrictive model or stitch partial refused output together with a fallback completion. Discard partial output from refused attempts and enforce consistent safety policy across all serving models.
examTip: Separate legitimate infrastructure failovers (5xx / network timeout) from policy refusals (`stop_reason: "refusal"`).

deck: Set 10: Responsible AI, Security, Guardrails & Governance
definition: To prevent automation bias (rubber-stamping), present human reviewers with **source facts and provenance**, extracted fields, explicitly **flagged policy gaps or conflicts**, and structured dispositions (`approve`, `edit`, `reject`)—rather than only showing a polished narrative.
examTip: Audit a random stratified sample of **automatically accepted** cases too; measuring only analyst overturn rate on escalated cases misses false negatives that bypassed review.

deck: Set 10: Responsible AI, Security, Guardrails & Governance
definition: When a pinned production model version approaches retirement, inventory all dependent services and provider mappings, benchmark the candidate replacement on workload-specific quality/refusal/latency gates per region, and migrate in verified cohorts with rollback contingency prior to the sunset date.
examTip: Pin explicit model snapshot IDs (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`) in production and never cut over 100% of traffic on retirement day without prior cohort validation.
